title: Tempo Lab two-week postmortem + next-cycle plan
content:
Purpose: quick personal postmortem for the last two-week micro-iteration (Tempo Lab). Use this as a scratchpad for what worked, what didn't, and what I want to try next. Not a team-level doc — my notes to surface during 1:1 and triage.

Sprint window: 2024-10-21 -> 2024-11-03 (14 days)
Primary personal objective: shrink feature delivery loop for the latency-adaptive batching spike (goal: get a production-proofed canary running end-to-end).
Key measurable outcomes I cared about:
- Canary end-to-end: deployed + smoke tests green (target: 3rd day)
- Unit cost reduction experiment: estimate cost/token down by >= 10% with batching tweaks
- CI flakiness: reduce CI flaky runs per week from ~6 -> <=2

Raw timeline notes (handy because I forget):
- Day 1: scoped canary + wrote deployment playbook draft, opened INF-2217 (incomplete tasks).
- Day 3: first canary deployed; discovered model-variant mismatch in routing rules -> rollback.
- Day 5: hack to fallback on compatible quantized variant; smoke tests passed locally.
- Day 7: flaky CI on integration tests (timeout on GPU warmup). Added retry and increased warmup timeout temporarily.
- Day 9: cost experiment with batching policy A/B started (small portion of traffic). Initial metric: 6% token-cost reduction but 12% tail latency increase.
- Day 12: adjusted batching parameters (prefill threshold) and added KV-prefix caching for hot prompts; tail latency improved.
- Day 14: closed most tasks, left a lingering TODO to formalize rollback policy and incident runbook.

What worked (notes to self):
- Fast prototyping of fallback variant was a good move — having pre-tagged compatible artifacts saved ~8 hours. Keep the "compatibility tags" pattern.
- Small-traffic A/B for cost policy was low-risk and produced actionable numbers. Will keep fractional rollout for infra-level changes.
- Local smoke harness is useful; expand to include warmup timing for GPU-backed tests. One-line task: move warmup timer config into test harness env.

What didn't work / surprises:
- I underestimated the routing policy semantics. A mismatch between the policy and the model catalog metadata led to the wrong-canary being picked. Need a validation step in the deployment pipeline that validates policy->model mapping.
- CI flakiness costed context switches. Current workaround (increase timeout + retry) is fine for now but masks the root cause (GPU warmup variability). Schedule a diagnostic: capture GPU initialization trace during CI runs.
- The initial batching policy produced worse tail latency than expected — my assumptions about request size distribution were off. Need better lightweight telemetry to infer request-size quantiles before changes.

Hypotheses to test next cycle (ranked):
1) If we gate aggressive batching behind a predictive-size estimator (estimate sequence length distribution per route), then we can preserve average cost wins and avoid tail latency regressions. (High priority)
2) Explicitly marking cold-start heavy routes and applying a different warmup/sharding policy will reduce CI flakiness and tail latency. (Medium priority)
3) Introducing 2-minute prewarming jobs during low traffic windows will reduce the number of cold-warm cycles and improve p95 for latency-sensitive customers. (Low priority / ops cost)

Concrete experiments to run (next two weeks):
- EXP-1: Build a lightweight request-size estimator (histogram over last 5k requests per route) and gate batching aggressiveness > threshold. Metric: p95 latency and cost/token. (Owner: me)
- EXP-2: CI diagnostic run: capture GPU init logs and process stack traces; correlate with flakes. (Owner: me + SRE buddy Ivy).
- EXP-3: Canary prewarm job experiment: schedule ephemeral prewarm jobs for the canary pool for 2 hours/day and measure change in tail latency. (Owner: Maya for ops coordination)

Quick metrics (back-of-envelope) from the last run:
- Cost/token (baseline): $0.00088 -> batching policy A: $0.00083 (6% reduction)
- p95 latency (baseline): 210 ms -> policy A: 236 ms (12% increase)
- CI flaky runs: 6 in last 2 weeks; 4 attributed to warmup timeouts, 2 to infra quota limits.

Open TODOs (practical, unglamorous):
- [ ] Add deployment-time policy validator in pipeline (INF-2217 follow-up).
- [ ] Add warmup-timer capture in local smoke harness and CI (write test harness task).
- [ ] Formalize canary rollback checklist + Slack paging steps (small runbook).
- [ ] Convert EXP-1 prototype into a lightweight service and instrument dashboards (screenshot examples in CONFLUENCE:TP-1423).

Stuff to bring to 1:1 with manager:
- Proposal to allocate one day of infra budget for a prewarm pilot (ops cost estimate included).
- Ask for 4 hours pairing time with SRE to decode GPU init traces.
- Clarify priority vs other backlog items: is canary stability higher priority than the embeddings cost optimization work? (I think yes for next 3 weeks.)

Notes to self / heuristics captured for future cycles:
- Always expect a model variant mismatch when composing routing + catalog changes; add a simple sanity check.
- Fractional rollouts are best for infra-level tweaks where cost vs latency tradeoffs are unknown.
- Distinguish CI flake masking vs real infra issues — don't patch with timeouts without a short diagnostic window.

Random friction / personal blockers:
- Felt mentally clogged mid-sprint (Day 6–9) — need to schedule 2x 45m deep-focus blocks on my calendar next cycle to preserve flow for the batching work.
- Context switching from support rotational shift slowed momentum on EXP-1; propose blocking support on my calendar for 3 days next cycle.

Next-cycle quick plan (two-week chop):
Week A (first 7 days): EXP-1 prototype + small dashboard; add policy validator skeleton to pipeline. Pair with Ivy for CI diagnostic late week.
Week B (next 7 days): Run EXP-1 in small canary, iterate based on telemetry, finalize rollback checklist, schedule 1:1 review with manager.

If I only get one thing done: ship the request-size estimator prototype (EXP-1) behind a feature flag and validate p95/cost on canary.

Final micro-retro (one sentence): learned that small compatibility artifacts and fractional rollouts save days — but without lightweight telemetry, cost experiments can easily regress latency.

Notes to self (quick bookmarks):
- CONFLUENCE:TP-1423 (dashboard mocks)
- JIRA:INF-2217 (routing-policy mismatch)
- GITHUB:rafi/tempo-lab#45 (prewarm job prototype)
